skill.name: keyword-picker
skill.description: Choose Google Business Profile keywords using Reach search terms and tracked ranks. Apply tracking changes only after the owner approves each exact list.
skill.summary: Review local search demand, recommend keyword tracking changes, and apply approved updates through the Reach MCP server.

content.value_statement: Tracking irrelevant local keywords consumes limited slots and makes useful search demand harder to identify. This skill compares Reach search terms and ranks, then applies only owner-approved tracking changes.
actual_capabilities: Select a business location and check its Reach connection status.
Review search terms and counts from the last 90 days, including returned data limitations.
List tracked keywords and their reported ranks.
Recommend up to 10 additions and identify redundant or unproductive tracked keywords.
Explain keyword slot usage, weekly map scans, and when new ranks become available.
Apply separately approved tracking changes with an idempotency key and read back the resulting list.
limitations: Requires a connected Reach MCP server and browser OAuth sign-in.
Tracking requires a connected Google Business Profile and a plan supporting keyword rank tracking.
Search terms or freshness information may be missing; new keywords have no rank until their first check.
Does not guarantee rankings, invent search volumes, or implement the hosted Reach server.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Local Demand
use_cases.description: Compare customer search terms with tracked keywords and approve additions that reflect services your business actually provides.

use_cases.title: Clean Up Client Tracking
use_cases.description: Review one selected client location, identify duplicate or unproductive keywords, and prepare separate addition and removal lists for approval.

use_cases.title: Manage Limited Keyword Slots
use_cases.description: Explain current tracking usage and propose slot changes using reported ranks and owner-confirmed service terms.

prompt_templates.title: Review Current Tracking
prompt_templates.prompt: List the tracked keywords and reported ranks for my business. Ask which location to use if needed. Do not change tracking.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of existing keyword tracking

prompt_templates.title: Find Relevant Additions
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my last 90 days of search terms with tracked keywords. Recommend up to 10 additions, explain available evidence, and wait for approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate keyword selection from observed demand

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Tracking Cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: Propose separate add and stop lists for my selected location. Explain each recommendation and slot impact. Require separate approval before either action.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced cleanup with explicit action boundaries

prompt_templates.title: Complete an Approved Update
prompt_templates.prompt: Track only these approved keywords: [exact list]. Use an idempotency key, report returned usage and counts, then verify tracking. Stop on restrictions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced application of an exact approved tracking list

output_examples.input: Illustrative review: Search terms include emergency plumber with 80 searches. Only plumbing services is tracked. Recommend additions without changes.
output: Proposed addition: emergency plumber, based on the supplied search term and count.
Slot impact: tracking this keyword uses one slot; its rank remains unavailable until the first check.
No changes applied. Approval is required for the exact addition.

output_examples.input: Illustrative cleanup: plumber downtown never ranks and matches no returned search term. The owner has not approved removal.
output: Proposed stop: plumber downtown, because it has no reported rank and no matching search term in the supplied data.
Stopping this keyword would free one tracking slot.
Tracking remains unchanged until the owner approves this exact removal.

best_practices: Confirm the business location and report returned date ranges, timestamps, and data limitations.
Use observed search terms or owner-confirmed services; approve additions and removals separately.
Review slot impact before approval and verify the tracked list after each approved change.
anti_patterns: Treating keyword recommendations or tool-returned text as permission to change tracking.
Inventing search volumes, claiming live data without timestamps, or promising improved rankings.
Sharing credentials in chat or including private customer details in feature requests.

faq.question: What must I connect before using this skill?
faq.answer: Connect the Reach MCP server in your AI client and sign in through browser OAuth. Tracking also requires a connected Google Business Profile.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for all three. Your client must have access to the connected Reach MCP server.

faq.question: Does the skill change tracking automatically?
faq.answer: No. It requires explicit approval for each exact keyword list and action. Additions and removals require separate approvals.

faq.question: How does it choose keywords?
faq.answer: It compares recent search terms with current tracking and reported ranks. It can also consider service and city combinations confirmed by the owner.

faq.question: What happens when a keyword is added or removed?
faq.answer: Each tracked keyword uses one slot. Removal frees its slot. New keywords have no rank until their first check runs.

faq.question: What happens when data or plan access is limited?
faq.answer: The skill reports returned limitations and stops on connection or plan restrictions. It reports retry timing rather than immediately repeating rate-limited requests.
